messages:
maya: Heads-up — ran a 2k-token MoE workload on 8xA100 and the profiler shows repeated all-to-all spikes that line up with token routing, causing ~30% GPU idle between layers. attaching quick flame timeline below.

chris: Can you paste the perf trace? is this inter-node or intra-node all-to-all?

maya: Intra-node for this run. Perf timeline (short):
```
[00:00:00] forward_layer_12: compute 12ms
[00:00:12] all_to_all_routing: 48ms (blocking)
[00:00:60] compute 9ms
[00:00:70] all_to_all_routing: 52ms (blocking)
```
GPUs 0/1/2 show repeating gaps.

dina: ouch. that 48-52ms all-to-all is huge. is routing using full-size tensors or chunked?

maya: current runtime sends full expert assignments per microbatch. no chunking. also KV cache writebacks are serialized after routing, so memory copies amplify the wait.

liam: two quick angles: (1) overlap communication with expert compute (start async all2all and proceed with local expert compute as soon as local inputs ready), (2) chunk the routing tensor into 4 parts to pipeline all2all + compute.

ana: @liam re overlap — we tried nonblocking collectives earlier but saw tail-heavy latencies because of stragglers. did we have per-GPU routing imbalance metrics?

maya: imbalance present. expert load skew ~3.2x between busiest and quietest. that plus large, synchronized all2all creates hotspot windows.

chris: two more levers: change routing policy to balanced-topk (approx) to avoid extreme skew, and try hierarchical all-to-all: do intra-socket then cross-socket to reduce bisection pressure.

perf-bot: profiling summary:
```
experiment: moe_run_1745
hosts: 1 (8 GPUs)
mean_all2all_latency: 49.1ms
stddev: 14.7ms
gpu_compute_util: 71%
gpu_idle_during_all2all: 29%
kv_memcpy_time_post_routing: 18ms
```

dina: KV behavior seems important — if we can avoid a full KV reshuffle per token batch (use local KV prefilling + delta updates) we can shave ~15-20ms. worth prototyping.

liam: agree. plan: try (A) chunked routing with 4-way pipeline + async all2all, (B) local-first KV caching to avoid global copy, (C) soft routing topk with threshold to reduce skew. 1 GPU each to run A/B/C for quick 10min runs.

maya: i'll run A on gpu0-1, chris take B on 2-3, dina take C on 4-5. collect perf-bot traces and reconvene.

chris: quick note on kernel selection: if we pipeline routing, we should force smaller GEMM kernels for intermediate batches to reduce tail latency — runtime flag kernel.policy=low-latency might help.

dina: adding: instrument a per-expert queue length metric and expose it in console so we can detect buildup pre-all2all.

perf-bot: scheduled experiments: A->1745001800, B->1745001900, C->1745002000. results posted to /eng-runtime/bench-reports.

maya: thanks — priority is to reduce peak all2all tail and KV memcpy. if anyone has a fast patch for nonblocking all2all + small-chunk sends, ping me.

liam: pinging @ana for possible NUMA-aware reorder for hierarchical all2all.

ana: on it, will prototype local-socket gather first.

chris: fyi, if chunking works we can also reduce routing metadata by compressing expert indices in-flight. small wins add up.

maya: great. reconvene after perf-bot posts traces. :thumbsup:
